LESSON: AREA

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.2 Length (6 lessons) • Conversions in length • Operations in leng
Topic 3.3: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of Measurements 3.2 Length (6 lessons) • Conversions in length • Operations in leng in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: What are plane figures? 2. How do we work out the areas of plane figures?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the relationship between square metre (m2 ) and hectares as units of measuring area

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. work out the area of a rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, and trapezium in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. work out the area of circles in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. calculate the area of borders and combined shapes in real-life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. recognize the use of area in real-life situations.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the relationship between square metre (m2 ) and hectares as units of measuring area

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. work out the area of a rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, and trapezium in different situations

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. work out the area of circles in different situations

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. calculate the area of borders and combined shapes in real-life situations

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. recognize the use of area in real-life situations.

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

2. use cut-outs to find the area of plane figures

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. generate conversion tables involving square metres and hectares as units of measuring area
2. use cut-outs to find the area of plane figures
3. watch videos on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner cuts out the circle into small sectors, joining them to create a rectangle

and generate a formula for getting the area of a circle.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner combines different shapes to make patterns.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner demonstrates how to derive the formula for the area of a circle.

Values

● Responsibility: as the learner cuts out the small sectors of the circle and joins them up to form a rectangle.

● Integrity: as the learner works out exact areas of different shapes.

● Unity: as the learner works in a team and shares tasks in measuring the area.

PCIs

● Safety: as the learner carefully handles different instruments/tools to make cut-outs of different materials.

● Environmental Education: as the learner uses locally available materials in measuring the area of different surfaces.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Creative Arts & Sports: as the learner combines different shapes to make patterns.

● Integrated Science: as the learner relates area to friction and pressure on a surface.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

1. identify the relationship between square metre (m2 ) and hectares as units of measuring area
2. work out the area of a rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, and trapezium in different situations
3. work out the area of circles in different situations
4. calculate the area of borders and combined shapes in real-life situations
5. recognize the use of area in real-life situations.

Remember the key question: What are plane figures? 2. How do we work out the areas of plane figures?
